intro.name: Ken Ashe
headline: Making sense of AI.
Making things with it.
intro.text: I explain AI in plain English and put it to work on real projects, from apps and videos to new business ideas. Follow along to learn something useful and see what I try next.
intro.positioning: A creator who makes AI understandable and explores what people can do with it through clear explanations, real projects, and stories from his own work.

homeAbout: I’m Ken. I spent about twenty years in finance and in project and product roles, and I’m a CPA and a PMP. Then I left corporate work to make things with AI and explain what I learn along the way.
This site is where the videos, projects and writing live. I also run Lucky Domains, which is a separate business.
draft.aboutLead: I’m an AI creator and builder based in New Jersey. I make AI understandable and explore what people can do with it, through clear explanations, real projects and stories from my own work.
aboutBackground: I started my career in accounting and finance, earning my CPA and working in financial reporting before moving into project, product and program leadership. Over roughly two decades I worked at S&P Global, EY, Noom and Prudential Financial, where I finished as Director of Project and Product Management.

Alongside that work I built digital businesses, including Lucky Domains, which I still run. I later left corporate work to focus on entrepreneurship and on making, and explaining, practical things with AI.

pillars.title: Understanding AI
pillars.text: Explanations, practical context, useful observations and opinions I’m willing to defend.

pillars.title: Creating with AI
pillars.text: Apps, videos, workflows, creative projects and business ideas, with what I made and what happened.

plain.zerohuman: A tiny online shop that only AI agents can use. They find it, pay it and get their order back with no person involved. It’s a small, real test of what business between AI agents could look like.
plain.returning-your-things: A two-minute short film made with AI-generated imagery and no dialogue. I wanted to see whether I could tell a whole story with only pictures and music.
plain.ai-agent-economy: I gave two AI agents their own crypto wallets and let one buy a service from the other. One real purchase, start to finish, that anyone can look up and check.
plain.ai-explainer-producer: An AI agent that researches a topic, checks the facts, writes the script and produces an explainer video with a virtual presenter. I tested it on a real explainer that I published.
plain.autonomous-seo-agent: An AI agent with a daily job: find five new places a website could be listed, set up the profiles and keep track of it all, without me stepping in.
plain.x-article-toolkit: A toolkit any AI agent can use to write stronger headlines, openings and cover images for X Articles, based on research instead of guesswork.
plain.ai-ugc-video-lab: An experiment in AI-made ads: 50 ad ideas built around one consistent character, ending in a made-up security campaign starring a raccoon.
plain.media-pitch-triage: A system that reads requests from journalists, scores which ones are worth answering and keeps track of what happened to each pitch.
plain.rebuilding-the-image-pipeline: How I rebuilt the way this website handles pictures, so pages stay light and the image files take up far less space.
plain.vetstack: A helper for military members and veterans that finds current discounts and benefits that actually apply, without asking for ID or a long list of questions.
plain.ai-werewolf: Nine AI characters with their own personalities and secret roles play a game of alliances, bluffing and votes. A fun way to watch how AI agents reason about each other.
plain.autonomous-ai-blog: An experiment in automated publishing: a system that reads the day’s AI news, writes articles and publishes only the ones that pass a quality check.
plain.geo-targeted-affiliate-site: A website that works out each visitor’s country and language and shows offers that fit, all generated from one spreadsheet.
plain.agent-driven-site-design-and-deployment: I had an AI agent build a real business website and put it online, from start to finish.
plain.sir-pitches-a-lot: An AI agent with one job: pitch Lucky Domains to possible clients. I built it in an afternoon and tried it live on a real target.
plain.kenashe-ai: This website. The first version was built in a day with AI coding tools.
plain.daily-email-to-myself: A morning email I built for myself: weather, markets, a dad joke and 300 words on a different topic each day.
plain.six-agent-email-response-team: A small team of AI agents that turns customer support emails into replies a person can review.
plain.personal-assistant-chatbot: A chat assistant that searches my email and answers questions about the weather and local news.
